entries.name: Spiritcaller
entries: Spiritcallers are a new phenomena in Prosperra. People born with an innate connection to the spirit world are not new but the amount of spirits around has never been higher.
This has led to the development of a new kind of magic, powered by the the spirits wandering Prosperra.
Rather than drawing the magic into themselves, Spiritcallers convince spirits to aid them or their companions, bonding them for a short time.
A Spiritcaller can also sever this connection, using some of the binding energy to cast a spell.
In contrast to the respected Wraithwielders, Spiritcallers are more on the fringes of society and in some places even actively persecuted.
As they struggle to find acceptance, Spiritcallers have begun to follow different paths, specializing in the many ways their bond with spirits can be used.

classFeature.name: Spirit Bonds
entries: Your connection to the spirits allows you to to establish temporary bonds.
When you finish a Long Rest, you choose a number of Spirits from the Spirit table equal to your Proficiency Bonus. You assign them to yourself or to a willing member of your adventuring party.
A person can be bonded to only one Spirit at a time, the bond lasting until their next Long rest unless prematurely severed by the Spiritcaller

A Spirit provides a benefit to the bonded person, each type of spirit confers a different type of benefit and the power of the effect depends on the proficiency bonus of the Spiritcaller. See the Spirit table for an overview

entries.name: Breaking the Bond
entries: As a Magic action, you can sever one of your active Spirit bonds. The bonded person must be within 30 feet of you, and you must be able to see them. You can also sever a bond you bear yourself.

When you sever a bond, its passive benefit immediately ends. You can then cast one spell from your spell list that belongs to the school of magic associated with that Spirit. The spell must be of a level equal to or lower than the level of the Spirit, as shown in the Spirit table.

The spell requires no spell slot. If the spell is of a lower level than the Spirit, the spell takes on the Spirit's level for that casting, as if you had used a spell slot of that level. This applies to any effects of the spell that depend on the level of the spell or the level of the spell slot used to cast it.
You otherwise follow the normal rules for casting the spell, including its components, Concentration, targets, and duration.
If the spell has a casting time of an action or a Bonus Action, the Magic action used to sever the bond is used to cast the spell.

classFeature.name: Spellcasting
entries: You have learned to channel spiritual binding energy into spells.

Certain spirits embody particular types of magical energy, and the process to learn how to attract a specific type of spirit and cast a spell from its energy requires considerable knowledge and practice.
As you gain experience, you can attract increasingly more potent spirits which can be used to cast more powerful spells.

entries.name: Bond Spells
entries: Rather than preparing spells normally, you select your Spirit bonds after every Long Rest. Each bond is associated with a type of magic, and severing the bond allows you to cast it a spell of that school of magic.
The amount and type of spirit bonds you can form is shown in the Spiritcaller Features table.

entries.name: Spellcasting Ability
entries: Intelligence is your spellcasting ability for your Spiritcaller spells.

You use your Intelligence whenever a Spiritcaller spell refers to your spellcasting ability. You also use your Intelligence modifier when setting the saving throw DC for a Spiritcaller spell you cast and when making an attack roll with one.
Spell save DC = 8 + your Proficiency Bonus + your Intelligence modifier
Spell attack modifier = your Proficiency Bonus + your Intelligence modifier

entries.name: Spellcasting Focus
entries: You can use an arcane focus, a spiritual focus, or a weapon with which you have proficiency as a Spellcasting Focus for your Spiritcaller spells.

classFeature.name: Weapon Mastery
entries: Your training with weapons allows you to use the Mastery properties of two kinds of weapons with which you have proficiency such as a Light crossbow or a Pistol.
Whenever you finish a Long Rest, you can change the kinds of weapons you chose.

classFeature.name: Fighting Style
entries: You gain a Fighting Style feat of your choice for which you qualify.
You can't choose the same Fighting Style more than once, even if you later gain another Fighting Style feature.

classFeature.name: Soul Mark
entries: Your connection to the spirits allows you to mark the souls of those you harm.
When you deal damage to a creature that is greater than its Intelligence score, you mark that creature's soul until the end of your next turn.
Each time you deal damage to a creature while its soul is marked, the mark's duration extends until the end of your next turn and its intensity increases by one.
As a Bonus Action, you can rend the soul of a creature you have marked. The mark ends, and the creature takes 2d6 Psychic damage for each point of the mark's intensity.
The creature can't take Reactions until the end of its next turn.

classFeature.name: Spiritcaller Aptitudes
entries: You choose an aptitude that determines the kind of relationship you cultivate with the spirit world.
Choose one of the following Aptitudes:

items: A Haunt, an expert in influencing peoples spiritual state by dreams and illusions.
A Spectre, whose connection to the spirits allows them to become one for a short duration.
A Soulmender, who understand and can manipulate the death/life divide.

entries: Your Aptitudes grants features at 3rd, 7th, 11th, and 15th level.

classFeature.name: Ability Score Improvement
entries: You gain the Ability Score Improvement feat or another feat for which you qualify.
You gain this feature again at 8th, 12th, and 16th level.

classFeature.name: Extra Attack
entries: You can attack twice, instead of once, whenever you take the Attack action on your turn.

classFeature.name: Spiritual Armor
entries: Your spirit can reinforce your body against harm.
When you take damage from an attack or other damaging effect, you can take a Reaction to reduce the damage by an amount equal to your Intelligence modifier + your Proficiency Bonus.
You can use this Reaction a number of times equal to your Intelligence modifier (minimum of once), and you regain all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest.

classFeature.name: Spectral Inquiry
entries: You have learned how to seek information from the dead and from spirits that linger in the world.
When you spend 10 minutes meditating on a specific question, you can attempt to contact a spirit that might know the answer.
Make an Intelligence (Arcana), Intelligence (History), or Intelligence (Religion) check against a DC determined by the DM.
On a success, you receive a cryptic indication of where or from whom useful information might be obtained.
The spirit does not necessarily answer the question itself.
On a failure, you receive no useful information.
Once you successfully use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a Long Rest.

classFeature.name: Spiritvision
entries: Your connection to the spirit world allows you to see the true spiritual energy of all living things.

items: As a Magic action, you gain Truesight with a range of 120 feet for 1 hour. Once you use this feature, you can’t use it again until you finish a Long Rest.

classFeature.name: Echo Step
entries: You have learned to briefly slip between the Material Plane and the spirit world.
As a Bonus Action, you teleport up to 30 feet to an unoccupied space you can see.
You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Intelligence modifier (minimum of once), and you regain all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest.

classFeature.name: Soulbreaking Strikes
entries: Your attacks can disrupt the spiritual cohesion of your enemies.
Once per turn when you hit a creature with a weapon attack, you can force it to make a Wisdom saving throw against your Spiritcaller spell save DC.
On a failed save, the target becomes Spirit-Broken until the start of your next turn.

entries.name: Spirit-Broken
entries: Its Speed is reduced by 10 feet.
It can't take Reactions.
The next attack roll made against it has Advantage.
A creature that succeeds on the saving throw is immune to this feature until the start of your next turn.

classFeature.name: Ethereal Step
entries: You can momentarily abandon your physical form.
When you are hit by an attack, you can take a Reaction to become partially incorporeal until the end of the current turn.
The triggering attack deals half damage to you.
Until the end of the turn, you can move through creatures and objects as if they were Difficult Terrain.
If you end your turn inside a creature or object, you are moved to the nearest unoccupied space and take Force damage equal to twice your Spiritcaller level.
Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a Short or Long Rest.

classFeature.name: Spirit Mastery
entries: Your bonds with the spirit world have become extraordinarily resilient.
When you sever a Spirit bond, you can choose to retain that Gift's passive benefit until the end of your current turn.
In addition, while you are within 10 feet of a creature carrying one of your active Spirit bonds, you have Advantage on Constitution saving throws you make to maintain Concentration.

classFeature.name: Epic Boon
entries: You gain an Epic Boon feat or another feat for which you qualify.

classFeature.name: Avatar of the Spirits
entries: You have become a living conduit between the material world and the spirit realm.
Whenever you roll Initiative, you can restore one Spirit bond that you previously severed during the current adventuring day.
The restored Gift returns to the creature that originally bore it, and its passive benefit immediately resumes.
Once you restore a Gift using this feature, you can't do so again until you finish a Long Rest.
In addition, while you have at least one active Spirit bond, you gain a +2 bonus to your Intelligence score, to a maximum of 22.

classFeature.name: Gift Types Known
entries: Your Gifts are manifestations of the spirits you have learned to commune with.
A Spiritcaller does not automatically know every Gift. Your Spiritcaller level determines how many Gift types you know.
At the end of a Long Rest, you choose which known Gifts to assign.
Each Gift has exactly one associated spell.
Severing a Gift casts that Gift's associated spell at the highest Gift Spell Level you can use.
